chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raised it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not incline towards those who are unjust, so the Fire would touch you', he said: 'He is the man who goes to the Sultan, so he loves his remaining until such time as he enters his hand into his bag and gives him something.'

key_terms.تَرْكَنُوا: To incline or lean heavily (with desire)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'And do not incline towards those who are unjust' mean in the context of political authority?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the verse 'And do not incline towards those who are unjust' (Hud 11:113) as a warning against the spiritual danger of seeking the favor of the ruling authority (Sultan) through subservience. He specifies that this 'inclination' manifests as a person waiting for the ruler to open his purse and grant a gift, highlighting the transactional nature of political loyalty in Shia jurisprudence. This hadith underscores the principle that accepting patronage from unjust rulers compromises the integrity of the scholar or official, a key theme in the chapter on 'Office-bearers for the Sultan'.
